svg.title: The Mixtape Archive, zine drawing
svg.desc: Fictional AWS architecture. The upload broker derives allowed tenant/object keys from verified identity and issues bounded temporary capabilities. The browser uploads; the identity arrow does not mean Lambda streams the audio. Cross-account workflow and MediaConvert roles need explicit source, destination and KMS policies. Job completion and human rights approval are separate preconditions; neither S3 presence nor successful encoding grants publication authority. Publication copies approved objects and updates the catalogue with reconciliation for partial failures. CloudFront origin access control authorizes private origin reads; signed viewer URLs separately authorize listeners. Master replication assumes source/destination versioning, replication roles, KMS grants and deliberate delete-marker/retention policies. It is asynchronous and is not a substitute for protected backups. No real music or rights claims are made. Artist identity to Scoped upload broker; Scoped upload broker to Quarantined masters; Quarantined masters to Authorized job workflow; Authorized job workflow to MediaConvert jobs; MediaConvert jobs to Unpublished renditions; Unpublished renditions to Rights and release gate; Rights and release gate to Approved playback files; Rights and release gate to Published catalogue; Signed CloudFront playback to Approved playback files; Quarantined masters to Versioned master replica. Boundary labels distinguish accounts, regions, VPCs, AZs, subnets and logical groups. These annotations do not verify deployed isolation or permissions.

g.title: Verified artist subject maps to an allowed tenant prefix; client-supplied object keys are not authority.
Broker grants a short-lived upload capability scoped to a server-selected object key; browser performs the upload.
Configured S3 EventBridge forwarding starts the cross-account workflow under a constrained role.
Scoped role submits an asynchronous job with explicit cross-account source bucket and KMS permissions.
Writes derived renditions; a completed file alone is not a published recording.
Successful job event plus human rights approval unlocks release; this is workflow progression, not S3 granting rights.
Release service copies approved assets through explicit cross-account read and destination write policies.
Catalogue becomes visible only after successful approved asset publication; reconciliation handles partial failures.
Origin access control and source-distribution bucket policy permit private reads; requests use signed viewer URLs.
Cross-account, cross-region S3 replication with versioning and KMS grants; deletion and retention policies are explicit configuration.
